voiceover:
[conversational] ChatGPT is just a chatbot until you plug it into your apps.

Stay till the end for the one permission you should never give it.

Composio connects 1,500+ apps, and its plan is free. The catch: ChatGPT needs a paid plan, and write access depends on which one.

On ChatGPT web, open Plugins, hit plus, then Add custom MCP server. Name it Composio, paste connect.composio.dev/mcp as the Server URL, accept the risk warning, then Create as a plugin. Open it, sign in to Composio, connect Gmail.

[playful] Now type @, pick the plugin, and ask: Read my 10 latest unread emails and add each lead to my Notion Leads database.

[serious] Here's the mistake: giving it full Gmail access when you only need triage. An email can hide instructions that steer the AI. Pick minimal scopes, keep send and delete toggled off, and read every confirmation.

Would you trust AI with your inbox? Send this to the friend who copy-pastes emails into Notion.

Hack saved?

pick.angle: ChatGPT is just a chatbot until you plug it into your apps. Here's the free way to do it, and the permission mistake to avoid when you give an AI access to your inbox.
pick.why: 594 comments on 21.8k views is about 2.7%, a very high comment rate for a niche automation topic. It's a business workflow with a free account and a real public site (composio.dev) we can show live. It also isn't covered in our recent list.

research.tool: Composio MCP server (https://connect.composio.dev/mcp) added to ChatGPT as a custom MCP server / plugin. This was previously called Developer Mode and Connectors.
research.availability: Composio: free Hobby plan, no credit card. ChatGPT side: NOT free. Custom MCP servers need a paid ChatGPT plan (Plus/Pro/Business/Enterprise/Edu), on ChatGPT web. Plan rules for write actions conflict between sources (see notes). Region limits not verified.
steps: Open ChatGPT on the web (a paid plan is required) and go to Plugins (chatgpt.com/plugins; also reachable via Settings → Plugins).

Select the plus button, then 'Add custom MCP server'. OpenAI's current docs no longer mention a separate Developer Mode toggle step, but older guides, and some Composio pages, still say Settings → Apps/Connectors → Advanced settings → Developer Mode. Check which your account shows.

Enter a name (e.g. Composio), set the Server URL to https://connect.composio.dev/mcp, and configure authentication as the form asks. Review the risk warning, select 'I understand and want to continue', then select 'Create as a plugin'.

Open the new plugin and authenticate: sign in to your Composio account (free Hobby plan) and approve the permissions. Then connect each app (Gmail, Notion, etc.) through Composio's Connect Link flow, choosing only the scopes you need.

Use it in a chat: type @ in the prompt box and select the installed plugin. Example prompt (Composio's own): 'Take this email from my CEO and create a Notion task with a due date.' ChatGPT will ask you to confirm any write action.
facts: OpenAI docs: custom MCP servers are added via ChatGPT Plugins → plus button → 'Add custom MCP server' → 'Create as a plugin'. ChatGPT supports both read and write tools. Supported protocols are SSE and streaming HTTP.
OpenAI docs: after setup, use the app in a chat by typing @ in the prompt box and selecting the installed plugin. In the plugin's settings you can toggle individual tools on or off.
OpenAI docs: 'Workspace permissions and security restrictions, including Lockdown, apply' to custom MCP servers. Custom MCP servers are 'not developed or verified by OpenAI'.
Composio MCP URL: https://connect.composio.dev/mcp (one URL; you connect apps behind it, so no second server is needed per app).
Composio's own site says '1,500+ more apps' (Gmail, Slack, GitHub, Notion). An older Composio article said '1,000+ pre-built toolkits'. 'About 1,000' understates it; '1,500+' is current.

Composio pricing (composio.dev/pricing, via secondary sources dated Oct–Nov 2026): Hobby $0, no credit card, 100,000 tool calls and 50,000 trigger events per month, 3 team members, hard cap. Usage pauses at the cap, with no surprise bill.
Composio Pro is $29/month and includes $29 in usage credit. Overage is $0.0003 per tool call.
Composio-managed OAuth apps have a smaller free allowance: 20,000 of the 100,000 tool calls (secondary sources).

Pricing changed on 15 Aug 2026 (old 20K/200K/2M tiers replaced); per-app credit pricing for managed apps applies to signups on/after Nov 3, 2026 (per pricing page). Ignore the older '20K free' figures.

Composio Gmail toolkit: its own article cites '63 available methods' for Gmail. A Composio article says Notion access is controlled at two levels: scopes chosen at OAuth, and which pages/databases you share with the integration.
Composio's own 'Email → Notion Task' prompt example is on composio.dev/product/composio-for-everyday-ai-users, so a Gmail → Notion workflow is officially demonstrated.
Composio guide: Notion on a team workspace may need approval from a workspace owner.
do_not_claim: 'Free' for the whole setup. Composio is free, but ChatGPT's custom MCP needs a paid plan. Composio's own article says free-tier ChatGPT accounts can't access the custom connector interface.
'One minute' as a verified time. No source confirms it. Composio's own Notion guide says 'under 15 minutes'. Say 'a few minutes' or 'three steps'.

'Developer mode in settings' as the first step, without a caveat. As of Nov 2026 OpenAI's docs use Plugins → Add custom MCP server. A third-party report cites OpenAI's help center as saying Developer Mode is no longer needed first and that you acknowledge a risk warning per server (not verified directly). Some Composio guides still show the old path.
'About 1,000 apps' stated as current. Composio's site now says 1,500+.
'Link in the Plugins section' as if you just paste a Composio link. You add the MCP server URL https://connect.composio.dev/mcp via 'Add custom MCP server', then authenticate.

'ChatGPT runs Gmail, YouTube and Notion by itself, no code'. A YouTube toolkit on Composio was not verified in this check. ChatGPT also asks for manual confirmation before write actions, so it isn't fully autonomous. 'Without code' is accurate for setup.
Any claim that Composio is an official OpenAI product or that OpenAI verifies it. OpenAI says custom servers are not verified by OpenAI.

Do not say all paid plans can write (send email, edit Notion). Sources conflict: one says Business/Enterprise/Edu only, with Pro read/fetch only, and another says Plus/Pro work. Say 'check your plan'.
criticism: Prompt injection: an email can hide instructions that steer the AI. With a write-enabled connector (send/delete/forward), a malicious email could trigger actions. OpenAI's docs list this as a risk and say custom servers are third-party and unverified.

Permission mistake to show: granting full Gmail scopes and write tools when you only need to triage. Safer: connect read-only/minimal scopes, keep tools like send and delete toggled off in the plugin's tool list, and never skip the confirmation prompt before writes. Read the destination in any confirmation.
A reported flaw (Tweakers, 8 Sep 2026, via a secondary source) showed attackers could use linked apps (Gmail, Drive, Teams, GitHub) through crafted prompts. Treat connected-app access as sensitive.

Data retention: Composio's zero data retention is an optional add-on, not included on the free Hobby plan (per pricing page, via a secondary review). Avoid sending highly sensitive mail through the free tier.
The free tier is hard-capped (100K tool calls). It is fine for personal use, but the cap pauses your workflows when reached.
Third-party MCP server in the middle: Composio holds your OAuth tokens and sees the data passing through it, so you are trusting a second company in addition to OpenAI and Google.

ui.platforms: Web only for adding the server (ChatGPT web, per OpenAI docs: 'Use ChatGPT on the web'). Desktop/mobile apps can use the plugin afterwards. Not verified in detail.
screens: I could not view live screens, so the layout below is from text docs and not pixel-verified. Labels are exact; positions are approximate.
ChatGPT web → Plugins page (chatgpt.com/plugins), a directory of plugins/apps. A plus button creates a new one. Selecting it shows 'Add custom MCP server'.

'Add custom MCP server' form: fields for a user-facing name and description; a 'Connection' section with the Server URL (or 'Tunnel'); an Authentication option (e.g. 'No authentication' or OAuth); a risk warning with a button 'I understand and want to continue'; then a 'Create as a plugin' button.

After creation: the plugin appears under your personal plugins. It lists the tools discovered from the server, each with a toggle, plus a refresh option. Open the plugin and select the plus button to install it.

Older UI (many guides still show it, and may still exist on some accounts): Settings → Connectors (or Apps) → Advanced settings → toggle 'Developer Mode'; then 'Create' with Server URL; a 'Developer Mode' option appears in the + menu in chat.
Auth step: a Composio sign-in/approval page opens, then Gmail's Google consent screen and Notion's access-approval screen. Gmail shows the requested permissions; keep them minimal.
Chat: type @ and pick the plugin. ChatGPT shows tool-call cards and asks for confirmation (approve/deny) before a write action. The result is the Notion task/page created or the Gmail labels/drafts.
Default theme: ChatGPT follows the system theme; not verified. Record in dark or light and keep it consistent.

research.visuals: Best shown as a real screen recording of the ChatGPT Plugins → Add custom MCP server form with the Composio URL, then a chat where ChatGPT reads a Gmail message and creates a Notion task, with the confirmation prompt visible. The final result is the new task in Notion. The pricing page and the OpenAI docs page can be used as B-roll proof.
research.notes: Verdict is 'adjust'. The trick works, but the transcript's claims are outdated or misleading. (1) The ChatGPT menu changed: as of Jul–Nov 2026 apps/connectors became 'Plugins', and OpenAI's docs say Plugins → + → Add custom MCP server. The old Developer Mode guide URL reportedly 404s, and some Composio pages still show the old Settings → Apps/Connectors → Advanced → Developer Mode path. Composio's pages also vary (Security and Login; 'ChatGPT Work'), so the writer should say 'Developer mode / Plugins' and show whatever the live account displays. (2) The 'free way' angle must be reworded to 'Composio's plan is free, but you need a paid ChatGPT plan'. (3) Plan conflict: one source cites OpenAI's help center as saying full MCP with write actions is only for Business/Enterprise/Edu, with Pro read/fetch only; other sources say Plus/Pro work in Developer Mode. I couldn't open the OpenAI help center directly, so state 'paid plan; write access depends on plan'. (4) Pricing figures: use the 100K calls/month free Hobby plan (hard cap, no card). Ignore blog posts that say 20K free, since they are outdated. Managed-OAuth apps have a 20K sub-allowance. (5) Suggested practical workflow: 'Read my 10 latest unread emails, label leads vs support, and add each lead as a row in my Notion Leads database'; start read-only for Gmail. (6) The caption's 'send GPT in comments for my materials' is a lead-magnet ad hook, so don't copy it. Note that the original reel's transcript was not available, so claims are inferred from the caption only.
